title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio, and Language
claim: A scene across modalities is bound into one shared representation that captures both what objects are and where they are.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right: inputs, central sphere, scene output; beam device
description: The figure reads left to right. On the left are three input modalities: a street photo of a white truck and a pedestrian, a binaural waveform with left and right ear icons, and a text box with a scene description and color-coded object clauses. Dashed colored lines link each input to a large central purple sphere labeled SceneBind. The sphere has orbital rings and a gray central cube for the global embedding, plus small colored cubes that stand for object slots. A pastel beam leads from the sphere to a line-art rendering of the street on the right. That rendering has a global scene cube at the top, object cubes pinned above the truck and man, and sound-wave arcs near them. Labels read 'Global Scene Semantics' and 'Object-Centric Semantic-Spatial Representation'. The eye goes first to the SceneBind sphere.
caption: SceneBind models scenes by jointly capturing semantics (what) and 3D spatial attributes (where) across vision, audio and language. SceneBind maps each modality into a shared global embedding with object-centric slots, enabling semantic–spatial representation of multimodal scenes.
abstract: We present SceneBind, an omni-modal representation of realistic scenes with joint semantic and 3D spatial understanding across vision, audio and language. Existing omni-modal encoders excel at instance-level semantics (i.e., what is present), but often lack explicit spatial structure (i.e., where it is). SceneBind addresses this gap by representing each scene as a semantic-spatial entity, combining a global semantic embedding with object-centric semantic-spatial slots. This representation explicitly captures object-level semantics, spatial attributes, and uncertainty. We further propose SceneBind Matching, a semantic-spatial matching scheme that integrates global scene similarity with object alignment, supporting cross-modal scene retrieval and object grounding. To train and evaluate SceneBind, we curate a novel real-world binaural audio-visual dataset with structured semantic and spatial annotations, and propose a training protocol for aligning semantic and spatial signals across modalities. SceneBind is compatible with large-scale pretrained semantic encoders, adds lightweight spatial modeling with only a few additional tokens. It achieves state-of-the-art scene and spatial retrieval while enabling strong zero-shot transfer to downstream tasks such as audio-visual localization.
